translationRepairs: Dou Tai, styled Shining Tranquility, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
Dou Tai, courtesy name Shining, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
字世寧 is a courtesy name; “Shining Tranquility” invents a semantic gloss absent from the Chinese, while courtesy name Shining restores the romanized 字.
Dou Tai, styled Shining Tranquility, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
Dou Tai, courtesy name Shining, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
Literal likewise invents “Shining Tranquility” for 世寧; courtesy name Shining matches the 字 without the false gloss.
He rose to three imperators' protocol of the open office.
位儀同三司 is the office Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes; “three imperators’ protocol of the open office” is a garbled mistranslation with no basis in the Chinese.
He rose to three imperators' protocol of the open office.
Literal repeats the same garble of 儀同三司; Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes correctly names the office.
As Wucheng sickened toward death, he entrusted the final testament to Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others alike — and made Dingyuan minister of works.
As Wucheng grew gravely ill, Dingyuan together with the Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others received the final testament; Dingyuan was made minister of works.
Preceding units concern 定遠; 與趙郡王等同受顧命 makes Dingyuan a co-recipient of the dying charge with the Prince of Zhao, not Wucheng entrusting the testament to Rui alone.
Soon he was removed and made Governor of Ying Province.
Soon he was appointed Governor of Ying Province.
尋除瀛州刺史 uses 除 in the appointment sense; “removed and made” invents a dismissal absent from the Chinese.

Once at the capital, Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou carried on with excessive ribaldry at court — and none of the nobles dared rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed; men praised Gan for it.

Once at the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei, carried on with excessive ribaldry at court — and none of the nobles dared rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed; men praised Gan for it.
魏譙王元孝友 is Yuan Xiaoyou holding the title Prince Qiao of Wei; fusing them as “Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou” muddles title and personal name.

Once when he visited the capital, Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou indulged in excessive ribaldry at court — none of the nobles could rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him; Xiaoyou was deeply ashamed, and contemporaries praised Gan.

Once when he visited the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei, indulged in excessive ribaldry at court — none of the nobles could rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him; Xiaoyou was deeply ashamed, and contemporaries praised Gan.
Literal has the same title–name fusion; reordering to Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei matches 魏譙王元孝友.
Earlier, Dingyuan's brother Jilue had a performing concubine. Mutipo demanded her; Dingyuan refused.
Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a performing concubine. Mutipo demanded her; Dingyuan refused.
定遠弟季略 uses 弟 for younger brother; adding “younger” restores the kinship marked in the Chinese without other change.
Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful. After Qi's fall she was given to Duke of Xue Changsun Lan.
Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful. After Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue.
薛公長孫覽 is Changsun Lan with the ducal title Duke of Xue; “Duke of Xue Changsun Lan” wrongly suggests Xue as a surname element.
Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Duke of Xue Changsun Lan.
Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue.
Literal likewise fuses 薛公 with 長孫覽; Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue correctly separates personal name and title.
Later, when Tang Junming, governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
Later, when Tang Junming, governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, he took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
唐君明居母憂，娉以為妻 continues Junming as subject of 娉以為妻; Shiwen did not take her as wife, though both were later impeached.
Later, when Tang Junming, Governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
Later, when Tang Junming, Governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, he took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
Literal repeats the reversed subject; 娉以為妻 refers to Tang Junming marrying during mourning, not Shiwen.
When Gao Yang succeeded to power, he held the Heyang garrison and routed Western general Yang Piao and others.
When Gao Yang succeeded to power, Le held the Heyang garrison and routed Western general Yang Piao and others.
文宣嗣事 is a temporal frame; the silent subject of 鎮河陽 and 破西將 is biographical Pan Le, confirmed by later 還鎮河陽 with 樂 as subject.
When Wenxuan succeeded to affairs, he garrisoned Heyang and defeated Western generals Yang Piao and others.
When Wenxuan succeeded to affairs, Le garrisoned Heyang and defeated Western generals Yang Piao and others.
Literal’s “he” after Wenxuan wrongly makes the emperor garrison Heyang; silent subject of 鎮河陽/破西將 is Le.
In the sixth year of Tianbao he died at Xuanchi.
In the sixth year of Tianbao he died at Xuanhu.
懸瓠 is the place-name Xuanhu (瓠 = hú); Xuanchi misreads the second character.
In the sixth year of Tianbao, he died at Xuanchi.
In the sixth year of Tianbao, he died at Xuanhu.
Literal likewise has Xuanchi for 懸瓠; Xuanhu restores the correct toponym.
